video_title: JWill says Anthony Edwards' legacy SHOULDN'T BE AFFECTED if the Wolves get bounced 🚫 | First Take

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' legacy shouldn't be affected by a second-round loss
quotes.quote: It wouldn't mean anything for him. Because he lost in the second round? After he hyper extended his knee? Have any of you'all hyper extended your damn knee? Have y'all seen that? Do you know what Giannis went through? And I know Giannis came back for a 50 plus point game in the NBA Finals. Do you know how hard it is to come back from hyper extending your knee to play at this level? I'm just saying, let's just put it in perspective, hyper extended knee, coming back, finding his way, and the success has been there before. I'm just not going to make it a big deal if Ant can't get his team over the hump this season. No excuses, I'm just saying.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: What a second-round loss means for the Minnesota Timberwolves' future
quotes.quote: Jay, here's what you're missing. I get where you're coming from. You missed the big picture in your answer. This ain't about Ant-Man in terms of what would a second-round loss mean for him? Here's the answer to that question. It means that he's seriously going to look at the Minnesota Timberwolves and say, what's my chances of winning here? That's where I'm going. It's not about him. The issue is how are we going to look at the Minnesota Timberwolves moving forward. Back-to-back years, you've gone to the Western Conference finals. Last year you got smacked around by OKC. This year when Wembanyama's on the court, San Antonio is smacking y'all around. Oklahoma City ain't going anywhere. They already got a crew. They already got Shai Gilgeous-Alexander locked up for years. The bottom line is, they've got assets out the wazoo. Oklahoma City's not going anywhere for the foreseeable future. And we all know this is officially the Wembanyama era. San Antonio's not going anywhere. So if you're Ant-Man in Minnesota, he doesn't have any hope in the foreseeable future of getting out the Western Conference. That's the point. And then when you look at a Karl-Anthony Towns, a person that you traded away to acquire, your Karl-Anthony Towns, you're averaging 14 now. This is not something that allows you to spring hope. No, that ain't happening here in Minnesota. So if you lose in this round, you're going to look at the future of the Minnesota Timberwolves and might ask yourself, is this the place for him to be?

quotes.speaker: Ryan Clark
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' superstar status debated among his young peers
quotes.quote: We talk about Ant-Man, I always hear, oh, he got this Jordan-esque quality about him, right? Let's talk about the Jordan-esque type people. You go Michael Jordan, you go LeBron James. Those were dudes who were the guys on their teams. They showed up in big moments and their team could never get over the hump. But look at who the people they lost to. They would lose to the Boston Celtics and Larry Bird. You lose to Isiah Thomas and the Detroit Pistons. If you're LeBron, you get to the championship and you lose to the San Antonio Spurs with Tim Duncan. There are all these teams who will be moving on and their stars will be aging out. That's not what's happening. You lost to Luka 4-1. He's still going to be around. You lost to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 4-1. And now you'll lose to Wembanyama. So we always talk about Ant-Man being the next up, being the next big superstar, but you're losing to people who will still be in your era for years to come. And so to me, that's what Ant has to get. Whether it's that number two that allows him to beat those level of players who are still young, who will still be playing, who will still be growing. That's what's important. His true superstardom to me is up for debate within his own era amongst his own peer.

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' lack of a veteran 'number one' sets him apart

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: You, Michael Jordan, who did Michael Jordan have to help him get over the damn hump? Who was his number two?

text_blocks.speaker: Ryan Clark
text_blocks.text: He didn't have anybody till he got Scottie Pippen.

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: Okay, okay, okay. When I put up that list, and I talked about notable players under 25 to reach three consecutive conference finals. The first was Kawhi Leonard when he was at the Spurs. Who was Kawhi Leonard's number one?

text_blocks.speaker: Ryan Clark
text_blocks.text: He came in with Tim Duncan.

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: Okay. Then I said Kobe. Who was Kobe's number one?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: Okay. Then I said Magic. Who was Magic's number one when he first came?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: All right. So all I'm saying, this dude's knocking on the door as number one. Who's his number two?

text_blocks.speaker: Ryan Clark
text_blocks.text: But my point to you was that's why I mentioned LeBron and Michael Jordan because they didn't have someone else that could carry them as a veteran. So they, but we put the same stress on them, like we did Peyton Manning.

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: I'm not putting Anthony Edwards in the same category as Michael Jordan and LeBron.

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Williams mocks Stephen A. Smith's 'hard' Western Conference argument
quotes.quote: Coming back to you, Mr. DC himself. Is it because things are getting hard in Minnesota? Now I have to take a chance and re-evaluate Minnesota because it's so hard in the Western Conference? It's so hard. You know, it's like where's OKC going? Oh man, they're so good and the Spurs are so good. It's hard. Maybe I should think about coming to the Eastern Conference. No. You would destroy somebody if they thought for one second, Stephen A, I know you. You are an absolute dog. You know what you did? When the rest of the networks got hard, you're like, you know what? I'm going to take a look at myself. We're revamping this entire thing. I'm bringing in studs. I'm bringing in Ryan Clark. I'm bringing in KP. I'm bringing Skip Bayless. I'm bringing on Cam'ron. I'm reinventing this. This is my house. Now you're talking, oh, I got to take a look at Minnesota and it's getting hard now. I got to, I don't know, I may go somewhere. No, you ain't doing that. I can't believe you just said that on national TV.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's playoff legacy defined by 'no-show performances'
quotes.quote: He can prove that all the things that have been written about him in games of this nature, that was the past and this is a different day and this is a different James Harden. We need to understand, Jay and RC, this is the game right here. I'm talking about Game 6 and a potential Game 7. This is it. What we saw from Harden, Harden did well last game, had 30 points, most of it came from free throws. I'm not judging that. The fact of the matter makes yourself effective, be aggressive and do what you have to do. Sometimes you ain't going to be accurate from the field. You're entitled, but you got to go for it. We got to remember that when we malign in any way James Harden, it wasn't because of bad performance, it was because of no-show performances. Last year in Game 7, this brother took nine shots. This is James Harden. We're talking about the absence of activity, the absence of aggression, which is so inexplicable because this is a guy that has the ball in his hands a vast majority of the time, that can get his shot off, that is a multi-time scoring champion and a former league MVP and one of the most prolific scorers we've ever seen in the game of basketball. Showing up in a Game 6 or 7 and you got an APB out for him because he's nowhere to be found even though reportedly he was in uniform and on the basketball court.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's history of 'unmitigated nightmare' playoff games
quotes.quote: It happened against San Antonio in the playoffs when he was in Houston. It happened against Golden State when he was in Houston. It happened against Boston when he was in Philadelphia. It's happened with him against Denver when he was with the Clippers. List goes on and on. You're looking at him and it's very, very anemic. And so it's usually the Game 6 or the Game 7 that this happens. And that's why I said tonight is so important because we've all been waiting. We've seen him perform well games one, two through four or five. It's the Game 6 and 7s that he's been an unmitigated nightmare. And that we got to find out whether or not he's going to be that dude. I saw what he did in Game 5. I was happy he did it. What you going to do in Game 6? You're back in Cleveland. You got an opportunity to close out the number one seed in the East on your home court after beating them on the road. And you got Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen, and Max Strus who showed up the other night with six threes to help you out. What are you going to do? We shall see.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Clark
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's legacy requires consistent elite play, not one game
quotes.quote: I don't believe it changes his legacy at all if he plays well in this Game 6. I believe people have made their mind up about who James Harden is. If this team doesn't win this game and then go on to the next playoff series and he play well and he shows up in Game 6 and in Game 7. You don't have this 17-year stretch of a career where you consistently in the playoffs and you don't win any titles and there's games like the 2020 game for the Rockets where he only scores 12 or you only score seven like you did last year. When those things happen repeatedly, you don't get to erase that away in one game. You don't get to erase that away in one night. Let's say he does play well tonight and we go into a Game 7 because Detroit does win. What would we be saying when the next game comes around? Who is James Harden going to be in this game? Because our experience with you is that when the biggest moments arise, you shrink. You become the smallest James Harden that we've ever seen. And to me, it's not just about the production, it's about the effort. It's about the look. It's about the aggression. It's about the want to. It's about the will. It's about the competitiveness. And you know this as well as anybody, Jay, for you guys, there's so much focus on the dude that has the ball in his hands, you got to tell me that I can count on you and I can believe in you. What's on the line for him tonight is to prove that in a new place to a new group of individuals, I can be that person.

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden faces 'nothing but upside' due to low expectations
quotes.quote: My answer to this question was, what's at stake tonight? Nothing but upside. Stephen A. used words, his player performance has been very, very anemic. Games sixes and seven have been unmitigated nightmares. That's the bar. That's the floor. So if we already know that's the case. If you're James Harden, if you're coming into this, you'll be like, okay, if I don't play well, y'all just going to keep saying the same old things y'all been saying. But if I play well, then I know I play well, but the goal posts are always going to move. So at some point if you're a player, you have to understand that, and I kind of made this post the other day. We value greatness by championships. I know that's our standard, right? When we think about the greatest of all times. James Harden is one of the most prolific scorers we've ever seen. I think the biggest thing for people to see more consistency with James Harden is all the attributes and intangibles you just made mention of. That when the games get that effort, that body language. That's the kind of stuff that you want to see him engaged in the game with. But as it relates to me, RC, like, ain't nothing but upside for him. Because people going to say the things they're always going to say.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden must perform at an elite level to change his narrative
quotes.quote: Jay is right in terms of the upside. But RC, I couldn't disagree with you more. If James Harden goes on a run, and let's say he plays on an elite level in Game 6, Game 7, they go to the Conference Finals, he does the same thing. He helps them get to the NBA Finals and he performs at an elite level. He is going to be looked at differently because how he's looked at right now. This is James Harden we're talking about here. This is a career like 24-point games. This brother is just lethal. He's elite at his best. He put up 30, he averaged 30 for seasons in the NBA, okay? We know what he did all those years in Houston. Then he got to Game 6s. In the last five Game 6s, James Harden's record is 1 and 4. He's averaged 16.8 points on 37% shooting and 23% from three-point range. This is James Harden we're talking about now. Game 7s, his last five Game 7s, his record is 2 and 3. He's averaged 14.6 points on 28% shooting from the field and 17% shooting from three-point range. Let me tell you something. It's one thing to have those numbers. It's another thing to exercise the eye test and to see what you're seeing. Literally watching a game and not knowing if James Harden is in it because he's been that quiet, that anemic, that impotent, that non-aggressive, and you look at him and say, what the hell is going on? Where is he? Damn, he's been in the game. Damn, he's played 30, 35 minutes. Damn, he's attempted that many shots. That's what, what is he doing? This is what you have asked for. If this brother performs in these games, these quality games, the Game 6 to 7s, oh, that changes the narrative about him.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Clark
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden needs consistent big-game performances to change legacy

text_blocks.speaker: Ryan Clark
text_blocks.text: We're talking about tonight. I said in my answer, if he plays well tonight, even if it goes to a Game 7, and then now you go to the series against the Knicks and he shows up. You can only change this perception. He can only change his legacy by consistency in the biggest moment. One night is not going to make you talk about James Harden differently, you talk about James Harden differently, or the world believe in him in this moment. He has to prove it in multiple Game 6s to me, and he has to find a way along with Donovan Mitchell and other pieces on the team that are good to compete for a championship. That's why they traded for him, not trade for him for just to be here in Game 6 against Detroit.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: How about this, RC? If he performed well tonight, we go from saying, oh damn, he ain't going to show up to, maybe he will show up. Because he did in Game 6. At least we do that. What I'm saying is, the narrative is, it's accompanied with an assumption that this brother ain't going to show up. He changes that. If he performs tonight, okay, maybe he will show up. Maybe he will.
